title: C:swim-divide: ringed Allen-Cahn cells from noise swim and divide with the link ring held through both (c07's ringswim with DL 0.2): seed 1 #563 swims 6.4 BL ringed and divides into two ringed swimmers
summary: c07's ringswim-waste-256 with the link mobility raised from 0.1 to 0.2, so links reach the wall before decaying. On 3 seeds at 256^2 a bounded population of walled cells forms from noise; labkit's aggregate L ring is 1.60-1.62 (147-170 cells membrane-like each), and a contour-distance ring score is >= 1.5 in 99.9% of cell-frames. 79-112 persistent splits (generation 14-15), 41-82 tracks swim >= 3 body lengths, all of them ringed. chi=0 removes the ring (median 1.11, 0% of frames) and cuts division 5x; mu=0 stops all swimming. Seed 1 #563 swims 6.4 BL with its ring and divides into two ringed daughters that swim 4.9 and 3.6 BL.

claims.statement: From smoothed noise over the whole domain (seeds 0-2, 256^2), walled Allen-Cahn cells carry a ring of their own link product at the wall (rim/core 1.60-1.62 labkit aggregate; contour score >= 1.5 in 99.9% of cell-frames), swim by their own phoretic drift (41-82 tracks >= 3 BL per seed, every one ringed) and divide (79-112 persistent splits, generation 14-15); individual lineages keep the ring through swimming and division.
claims.track: seed 1, ringtrack #563 (img/strip_s1_563.png, img/div_s1_563.png, data/rt256_s1.report.txt): ring 1.81-2.31 in every scored frame while it swims 6.4 BL (t=14540-17900), pinches at t~17920 into #665 and #666, which keep the ring (100% of frames >= 1.5) and swim 4.9 and 3.6 BL

controls_run.B: data/rt256_chi0_s0.* (chi=0, seed 0: ring median 1.11, 0% of cell-frames >= 1.5; persistent splits 20 vs 96)
controls_run.M: data/rt256_mu0_s1.* (mu=0, seed 1: 0 tracks >= 3 BL; ring and 80 persistent splits remain)
